Impute compositional zeroes

Source: R/comp_impute.R
comp_impute.Rd

Replaces zero values in a set of composition parts using one of the continuous imputation methods of zCompositions. declare_composition() calls this function on the raw (pre-closure) scale, before it closes the composition.

Usage

comp_impute(
  data,
  parts,
  method = c("lrEM", "multRepl", "lrDA", "multLN", "lrSVD"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the composition parts.

parts

Character vector of column names making up the composition.

method

Imputation method: "lrEM" (default, log-ratio EM, zCompositions::lrEM()), "multRepl" (simple multiplicative replacement, zCompositions::multRepl()), "lrDA" (log-ratio data augmentation, zCompositions::lrDA()), "multLN" (multiplicative lognormal, zCompositions::multLN()) or "lrSVD" (SVD-based, zCompositions::lrSVD()). "multLN" is called with rob = TRUE (the ROS-based alternative) unless rob is supplied through ...; its classical-MLE default (rob = FALSE) fails inside comp_impute() with "could not find function \"survreg\"". zCompositions::multKM() (Kaplan-Meier based) fails in the same way and is not offered.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to the chosen method (most usefully dl, to override the derived per-part detection limit, or a method-specific control such as lrEM's rob/tolerance/max.iter). The internal defaults (label = 0, the derived dl, and suppress.print = TRUE where the method accepts it) fill in only the arguments not supplied.

Value

A list with elements parts_imputed (a tibble: the zero-free parts on the original scale), imput_table (a tibble summarizing zero occurrence per part: part, n, n_zero, pct_zero, min_nonzero), and impute_method (the method used, or NA_character_ when no part had a zero). When no part has a zero, parts_imputed equals the input parts columns unchanged and no imputation method is called.

References

Palarea-Albaladejo, J., & Martín-Fernández, J.A. (2015). zCompositions – R package for multivariate imputation of left-censored data under a compositional approach. Chemometrics and Intelligent Laboratory Systems, 143, 85-96. doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2015.02.019

See also

declare_composition(), which calls this internally.

Other declare and describe composition: comp_outliers(), declare_composition(), plot.compD(), summary.compD()

Examples

cd_data <- timeuse
cd_data$MVPA[1:3] <- 0
imp <- comp_impute(cd_data, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"))
imp$imput_table
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   part      n n_zero pct_zero min_nonzero
#>   <chr> <int>  <int>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 MVPA    300      3        1         0.1
#> 2 LPA     300      0        0        51.8
#> 3 SB      300      0        0       316. 
#> 4 SPT     300      0        0       240.
